description: A judge's choice of one candidate from the candidates it was exposed to, with an assessment of every one of them. The integrity property is that a judge may only select from what it was exposed to: one subject per declared candidate port and no others. Non-candidate inputs may be exposed alongside them — a base repository, a rubric, a prior review — but are not selectable and must not appear as subjects.

body/selected.label: Selected
body/selected.description: The id of one of this record's own candidate subjects. The domain is closed; the pick inside it is the judge's whole job.

body/candidates.label: Candidates
body/candidates.description: Required, unlike every other entity-set in the six types: the subject set is non-empty and the candidates must assess every candidate subject exactly once, so an absent candidates array can never be valid.

body/candidates/*/scores.label: Scores
body/candidates/*/scores.description: The score dimensions are the judge's own; no closed set of dimensions exists, and an assessment may carry none.

body/candidates/*/scores/*/score.description: Unpinned, unlike a diagnosis confidence: any of the three scales and any of the three directions is legal here, so bounds and target are optional rather than forbidden. Optional does not mean unconstrained — which of them must appear depends on the sibling scale and direction the record itself chooses, and that is the referenced Go rule.

go_only_rules.rule: Candidate ports come from the workflow function's own port declarations at seal time, and from the sealed candidate-role subjects at read time, because a reader holds no declarations. Inferring candidacy from producer-written subject roles at seal time is rejected outright: a producer's claims never create authority.
Each declared candidate port must have one subject, every subject must bind a candidate port, and every subject must carry the candidate role.
All candidate subjects must have one common snapshot type, so a selection never compares unlike things.
The candidates array must have exactly as many entries as there are candidate subjects.
Every candidate id, and the selected id, must name a candidate subject this record declares.
Candidate ranks must be unique and lie within 1..N for N candidates; the ordering itself is the judge's.
The selected id must appear exactly once in the candidates array.

A unit-interval score's value lies within 0..1 and declares no bounds; a bounded score requires finite ordered minimum and maximum containing both the value and any target; an unbounded score declares no bounds; a target direction requires a finite target and the other two directions forbid one.

Turning the selection into a live snapshot reference needs the step's input bindings, which exist only while the step runs. A reader instead reads the chosen subject's type and digest out of the sealed bytes.
